dimensions.definition: How the metric-bearing task is decomposed into learned subproblems and what each prediction means.
dimensions.boundary: Does not own input encoding, model topology, loss implementation, or the fixed evaluator.

dimensions.definition: How allowed raw examples are acquired and which examples or external sources belong to the training or auxiliary pools.
dimensions.boundary: Does not own within-example transforms, derived synthetic variants, exposure frequency/order, or validation folds.

dimensions.definition: How one raw example becomes the canonical model input.
dimensions.boundary: Does not own stochastic training-only views, the learnable predictor, or inference-time search.

dimensions.definition: How extra training examples or views are derived or synthesized from allowed information.
dimensions.boundary: Does not choose external source membership, reusable supervisory signals, or test-time augmentation.

dimensions.definition: How learning signals are produced and attached to examples.
dimensions.boundary: Does not define target semantics, scalar loss aggregation, or the optimizer.

dimensions.definition: The learnable function class and its structural organization.
dimensions.boundary: Does not own pretrained weights, the trainable subset, or aggregation of separately trained predictors.

dimensions.definition: Where parameters start and which parameters or added adaptation mechanism are trainable.
dimensions.boundary: Does not own the base function topology or time-varying freeze/unfreeze phases. A task-fixed base model is represented as baseline-only.

dimensions.definition: Which scalar criteria define a good update.
dimensions.boundary: Does not own the fixed task metric, the origin of labels/rewards, or the update algorithm.

dimensions.definition: How gradients or other learning signals produce one parameter update.
dimensions.boundary: Exact numeric settings belong to inner HPO; phase ordering, stopping, and low-level execution do not.

dimensions.definition: How data, objectives, and trainable regimes are sequenced under the budget.
dimensions.boundary: Does not own pool membership, the update equation, validation estimators, or semantics-preserving acceleration.

dimensions.definition: Which training-only evidence selects configurations or checkpoints and decides when to stop.
dimensions.boundary: Does not include the immutable official evaluation or HieraResearch's outer point-selection policy.

dimensions.definition: How multiple independently usable trained predictors are combined.
dimensions.boundary: Jointly trained branches belong to architecture; repeated views or decoding from one predictor belong to inference.

dimensions.definition: How fixed predictor(s) are invoked to produce raw predictions.
dimensions.boundary: Does not own multi-model combination or conversion of raw predictions into final task outputs.

dimensions.definition: How raw predictions become the metric-facing decision, submission, or model artifact.
dimensions.boundary: Does not alter predictor execution or the official scoring rule.

dimensions.definition: How the same intended method is realized within time, memory, hardware, and dependency constraints.
dimensions.boundary: If a change intentionally alters examples, updates, or predictions, it belongs to the corresponding statistical dimension instead.
